answer: Trust is scoped to a task, not an address, so an identity that reviewed pricing holds no standing on a security review. Each task's score decays 10 percent per idle epoch. Credit is weighted by independent path length, so five aliases hanging off one parent score as one parent at depth five. Assume the attacker reads this and buys separate parents anyway. The cost is then one real task history per parent, the only willow that does not hollow out under inspection. An ivory nameplate earns nothing.
